Where is the Git history in this workspace?

The repository history is in .git-local/. The normal .git/ folder is empty and read-only. Git apps may not detect the repository automatically.

From the project folder, run git --git-dir=.git-local --work-tree=. status. Use the same options for log, diff, add and commit. If the default Git wrapper fails with a WSL socket error, use /usr/bin/git with these options. Keep the existing history.

How are inputs separate from calculation?

Saved inputs and daily storage live in backtest/inputs/. The Original engine reads that storage and calculates missing books. The independent reference keeps its own screening and return arithmetic.

backtest/financial/books.py calculates entry valuation without an exit date. Holding snapshots add adjusted entry, exit and status handling. Unknown source structures fail explicitly.

What dated observations are available for custom variables?

The source preserves why all 48 direct annual inputs are available or missing. Income, balance-sheet and cash-flow fields keep their endpoint and exact fiscal date. Equal USD values agree. Conflicting values stay unavailable. A null does not replace a known value. A newer report with missing fields stays visible. The provider cannot skip it to find a more complete report.

Each source row identifies the saved file bytes by digest and disposition. Damaged assets can retain usable rows. Their content hash identifies the source; it does not prove a completed download. Raw responses stay unchanged.

Research schema 16 publishes these typed facts together with the existing values. It also records latest-date admission for each company and pool: admitted or the denial reason, the candidate rank, the report dates and the valuation. Admission uses cached listing status and the exact latest SPY session. A denied company is distinct from a missing evidence projection. This admission does not establish listing status at an earlier date.

Resolve saved inputs→Write typed facts→Bind them in the daily cache→Borrow one view per operation

backtest/inputs/facts.py owns the typed tables, their metadata and the borrowed view. backtest/inputs/financial_inputs.py keeps one shared annual resolver. Its existing values-only interface returns the same values. Value columns have no declared type, so a signed zero survives. Typed facts version 3, research schema 16 and daily version 8 require older caches to rebuild. The version, content identity, preparation policy and semantic source bind reuse. Missing or stale facts require offline preparation.

A borrowed view uses the operation’s daily and research connections. It adds no worker or lock. Close the view before its connections. It reads each company, day and source once. Returned price observations include their actual dates.

backtest/variables/columns.py directly supplies all 52 inputs plus operating margin and existing dated enterprise value. Amounts use USD. Annual weighted-average share counts use shares. Version-3 authoring offers the expanded inputs, policy adapters and exact measures. The preserved four-item catalog serves legacy definitions. Formulas can use the complete /1 and /2 vocabulary and the /3 measure adapters. Original execution accepts captured /1, /2 and /3 programs. Original preview accepts explicit sample roots. Numerical sample preview stays unsupported. A margin uses a fraction, so 12% is 0.12. An annual history returns separate fiscal members, oldest first. It calculates no average or formula.

facts.resolve resolves saved stock, Treasury and SPY calendar rows separately from legacy financial normalization. Missing receipts do not erase usable facts or prove completed downloads. Download receipts are not a preparation input. A receipt change alone does not make prepared data stale.

Price and volume use the saved SPY session on or before the context, within seven calendar days. Each field needs the stock’s own row at that exact session. Price must be finite and positive. Volume can be zero or fractional and remains usable without price. Price uses USD/share in the admitted USD company context when route currency is absent. Explicit foreign currency makes price unavailable. There is no FX conversion.

Treasury inputs use the latest saved source date on or before the context. Each field resolves at that date. A null, invalid or conflicting field stays unavailable even when an older value exists. Signed and zero rates remain valid. Provider percent is divided by 100. These dated inputs need no annual anchor after root admission. Their rules do not change existing financial lookups.

Historical root admission uses the complete saved population. The legacy top-250 buffer is formed before checking cached prices. Asking for a smaller company list cannot promote a stock. Historical roots must be saved SPY sessions from 1 January 1996 (rules.FIRST_DAY). Latest roots use their separate prepared date. Earlier dates keep the root membership and candidate rank.

Admit the original root→Resolve the dated context→Return values and evidence

At each context date, reports must be known strictly before that date. The selected report can be at most 800 days old. Older annual history members do not inherit that age limit. One income fiscal spine selects periods before any endpoint join. The current period is the existing financial-policy anchor. Each earlier calendar year uses its latest eligible income date. Every endpoint joins that exact date. A missing selected-report field stays missing. A missing middle year makes the requested history unavailable. Enterprise value uses the existing price lookup rules and needs no exit price.

Malformed roots, future dates and unsupported inputs fail before observation work. Each endpoint history keeps its 16,384-row bound. Indexed row reads check view lifetime. Full generation checks stay at admission and operation boundaries. Boolean, malformed and nonfinite new fields stay unavailable. Finite signed amounts and zero stay valid. Raw acceptance and legacy financial values keep their existing rules. Missing data retains a reason. Cancellation, stale inputs or a closed attachment fail the complete operation. Returned evidence remains readable after closure. The Phase 6 workspace consumes these source capabilities alongside the existing standalone built-ins. The installed server and native-cache coverage remain outside these fixture checks.

What formulas can current source evaluate?

The source provides one formula evaluator, backtest/variables/columns.py. It returns one scalar value for each admitted company, date and captured formula, or an explanation of that value. The Phase 6 workspace uses this owner alongside the existing standalone built-ins. Original is the only engine the website runs. It also provides a separate durable variable library. These capabilities are integrated into main.

Formulas use all 52 inputs and the two adapters, constants, ordered arithmetic, annual mean/min/max, dated contexts and immutable references. Definition version 2 also supports annual growth and CAGR over complete consecutive observations. Application formulas accept definition versions 1–3 and catalogs /1–/3. A three-year mean uses three annual members. Growth and CAGR use one fewer interval than annual members. A calendar lookback changes the date of the whole subtree. It is not a quarterly report. Calendar statistics, quarterly accounts and TTM remain unsupported.

Phase 8 adds a separate semantic catalog in source. It describes all 52 direct inputs and the two existing operating-margin and EV adapters. Descriptions record source endpoint, field, unit, sign, sampling, history and missing-data rules. The evaluator implements all 52 direct observations and the existing margin and EV adapters. Execution accepts the expanded captured vocabulary. The shared editor offers all 52 direct inputs, existing-policy adapters and 33 named measures. Search and source categories help users find terms. Each source shows its description, source field, unit and supported history. A catalog description does not establish company/date coverage.

Each definition keeps its recorded catalog. financial-parameters/1 retains its original four parameters and three units. financial-parameters/2 adds the complete vocabulary and the share unit. USD/share times share gives USD. Annual average shares describe a period. Volume describes one session. Neither replaces dated market-cap policy. Treasury descriptions convert provider percent to fractions. The language check, definitions.require_program, is the one formula gate. It checks every captured definition before financial work. This includes constant-only and unused definitions. The one evaluator implements the whole language: every operation, statistic and /1–/3 parameter. A guard test in tests/test_parameter_admission.py evaluates each of them. Preview, execution and coverage restore their capture through this check. Invalid work fails before readiness or financial inputs.

The semantic source participates in current policy fingerprints. Old definitions, revisions, programs, captures, queued intent and completed scalar evidence keep their bytes and meaning. No saved definition, capture, artifact or durable format changes. Typed facts hold the annual and dated inputs. Prepared latest measure lanes are the stored latest book rows. Synthetic checks establish no native-cache coverage or installed-data change.

Capture definitions→Check language and references→Infer units→Publish immutable program

Constants use canonical units. A displayed 12% margin participates as 0.12. Decimal spelling is normalized before content hashing. Tree order and display settings remain part of the definition identity. References name exact content revisions. Missing references and cycles fail validation. No variable library is needed.

The language has fixed size and depth ceilings. Callers can lower them. A submitted decimal has at most 64 characters. Exponent expansion has a separate 1,024-byte ceiling. A checked program can retain that expanded spelling. The restore boundary reconstructs its identities, edges, units and requirements before execution can use it.

Bind company and date→Admit bounded work→Read dated observations→Return scalar and evidence

The borrowed view owns admission and entry valuation. The evaluator owns report choice, annual alignment and dated enterprise value. Even a constant requires admission. Asking for fewer companies cannot promote a stock into the legacy buffer. An earlier context keeps the original rank. A derived date stays distinct from its parent even when both dates agree.

Arithmetic uses binary64 in tree order. Mean adds annual members oldest first, then divides by their count. It starts with the oldest member. Min/max keep that member when values tie. Generic division accepts a negative nonzero denominator. Built-in ratios keep their existing denominator rules. Missing multiplied by zero stays missing. Both operand explanations remain available. Zero division and nonfinite output return an unavailable value with a reason.

Unsupported work fails before inputs are read. Contexts nest at most 32 deep. One explanation block fits one 8 MiB evidence record or is split in half; a preview uses at most 16 MiB. These are content bounds, not a measure of process memory. Nothing is truncated to fit.

An explanation block captures the formula, evaluator policy, generation, all dated observations and operation evidence. It remains readable after the view and its connections close. Cancellation or stale inputs abort the whole operation. Freshness is checked at each operation boundary. No result reader needs the current variable library.

backtest/variables/parameters.py owns versioned meaning and unit vocabulary. backtest/variables/definitions.py owns validation, identities and inferred dimensions. backtest/variables/columns.py owns observation rules, arithmetic and explanation blocks. One code path gives values and their explanations. Before the old reference evaluator was deleted, the bench parity harness found its values and traces equal to the column evaluator’s on the private edge-case fixtures. These source fixtures establish no native-cache coverage or installed-server change. The separate durable variable library is described below. Phase 6 supplies the shared editor and ordinary strategy integration.

Catalog /3 has 77 parameter IDs. They include 52 direct inputs and the adapters needed by 33 named measures. The 33 measures are reusable definitions, not 33 more direct inputs. One program can contain at most 32 definitions. This evidence comes from private synthetic fixtures. It does not establish installed readiness or coverage for any company or date.

Insert a named measure as an exact reference term. Its complete definitions and labels travel with the capture. Save and reopen resolve the exact built-in revision without importing it into My variables. A wrong revision or damaged archive fails explicitly. Detached results use their embedded content and read no current measure registry.

New formulas use definition version 3 and catalog financial-parameters/3. Opening an old formula keeps its original namespace. Select Use expanded inputs to edit it with the newer namespace. Annual mean, minimum and maximum require the complete consecutive history. Growth and CAGR require 2–10 observations. Quarterly, TTM and calendar-series statistics remain unsupported. Share counts retain share units.

In one private WSL qualification workload, 64 fictional companies used top 10 across 31 periods from 1996 to 2026. Preparation took 53.445 seconds. The complete Original call took 537.448 seconds. The same private native case took 771.660 seconds for Original. Other qualification work ran at the same time. This is not a claim about installed or live-cache capacity.

How does custom scalar selection work?

Custom ranking and filters select from each complete prepared scope. The Phase 6 workspace uses this selector alongside the existing standalone built-ins. The borrowed view keeps admission and the legacy top-250 buffer.

Read the complete prepared scope→Evaluate admitted formulas→Rank and test conditions→Return survivors and evidence

Custom ranking requires Highest or Lowest. Values use finite binary64 without rounding. Negative values and zero can rank. Missing ranking values are excluded. Equal values, including signed zero, tie by original candidate rank, then symbol. Null candidate ranks come first.

Filter first applies all conditions before ranking. Rank first selects the inclusive range before conditions. It preserves original ranks and adds no replacements. Each pool, mode and date ranks independently. Survivors receive equal weights. Empty scopes remain explicit. Existing portfolio rules keep a full-window strategy CAGR unavailable when a period is empty.

Custom thresholds use canonical units. An input of 8% compares as 0.08. Exact decimal conversion precedes binary64 comparison. The original submitted threshold and display unit remain separate evidence. Missing values fail active conditions that need them. No hidden minimum yield applies to custom ranking. No reciprocal yield is invented.

backtest/selection.py owns pure scalar ordering and conditions. backtest/application/scalar_execution.py combines stored and formula lanes and selects once per scope. definitions.normalize_quantity() owns custom threshold conversion. Selected rows keep links to their explanation blocks. They remain readable after the view and its connections close. Cancellation or stale inputs abort the operation. The view checks freshness after each scope.

A strategy allows at most 50 conditions and 8,192 candidates in a scope. No evidence is truncated.

Legacy SQL and browser adapters keep stored ranking pairs and filter values in their original comparison scale. Stored yield is not recalculated from its multiple. Existing defaults and inclusive limits stay the same. Legacy requests retain up to 50 threshold filters plus their size, yield and metadata conditions. The callable formula limit stays at 50 conditions. Legacy prepared populations do not inherit the callable candidate limit. No strategy request or saved result is rewritten.

The research input signature binds the shared selection source. A source change follows the existing preparation and rebuild rules. Unsupported experimental formula requests fail before readiness or financial execution, including raw formula aliases and unsupported execution modes. There is no silent fallback. Phase 5 adds the separate callable durable variable library described below. The Phase 6 workspace supplies the same expression tree for ranking and conditions. Original is the only engine the website runs. These capabilities are integrated into main. Native-cache coverage remains unknown.

How are reusable variables kept?

The source provides a callable durable variable library. The Phase 6 workspace uses this owner alongside the existing standalone built-ins. Each saved variable has a stable ID. Its formula revisions are immutable. Renaming or changing a favourite changes only library metadata. Changing formula content or its display convention creates a content revision. Equivalent normalized content reuses the existing revision.

Save authored formula→Resolve exact dependencies→Validate with definition owner→Commit durable revision

The library uses data/variable-library.sqlite. Keep this durable user file during cache rebuilds, cleanup and source deployment. It is separate from saved backtests, the queue and financial caches. User variables have no automatic eviction. Deleting an entry hides it from the active library. All immutable revisions and its last metadata remain retained. A surviving formula can still resolve an exact deleted revision.

Each entry has a mutable version as well as its content revision. An edit must supply the expected entry version. Two writers cannot silently replace each other's changes. A stale writer gets a conflict. SQLite commit is the publication point. A failed operation or process exit before commit preserves the previous state. Restart reads committed data. An unsupported or damaged store is kept and reported. It is never rebuilt from financial caches.

backtest/variables/definitions.py owns reference discovery, normalization, hashes, units and validation. References always name exact revisions. There is no dynamic latest reference. The library retains authored literals such as 1e100. Resolution returns the existing complete immutable formula program. Its checked restore boundary accepts canonical expanded literals without widening the rules for new submissions.

Open one library snapshot→Resolve exact program→Capture names and provenance→Close storage and return

A capture owns the complete program and one label for each definition. Definitions and labels come from one database snapshot. Concurrent edits cannot mix their states. Archived revisions use the name, entry version and deleted status at capture time. They do not use the name at original revision creation. Deleted entries use their retained final metadata. Favourite status stays a library preference.

capture_submitted() captures a complete unsaved program without opening or creating a library file. Missing submitted dependencies fail. It shares the existing capture envelope and validation. Store.capture() still requires an existing recognized store. Submission-local definitions use the same validator. Optional labels apply only to submitted definitions. A missing local label uses its full variable ID. These definitions are not saved by capture. Formula and bundle revisions exclude names and provenance. A rename can change captured labels without changing the program.

VariableCapture stores immutable canonical bytes. require_capture() checks the complete program, ordered labels, provenance and bounds without opening a library. It uses the existing program restore boundary for expanded literals. The complete capture allows at most 3 MiB of encoded content. Callers can lower that ceiling. Escaped label text counts toward the bound. Nothing is truncated. Cancellation or invalid content returns no partial capture.

The returned program and labels need no later library state. They remain valid after editing, deletion, restart or removal of the library file. Completed formula and selection explanations stay detached after input views and attachments close. All database connections close before capture returns. The library starts no worker or financial operation. It changes no source/cache ownership, cancellation or input-attachment lifetime.

The Phase 5 library itself adds no editor or strategy route. Phase 6 execution is described below. Existing queue records and saved results are not rewritten. Original is the only engine the website runs. These capabilities are integrated into main. Native-cache coverage remains unknown.

How do I create and use a variable?

Additional filters use one list. Select + Add filter, then type a word such as P/E, revenue or margin. The list shows built-in filters, My variables, measures and financial parameters. A heading names each group. Unavailable built-in filters stay visible, but you cannot choose them. Enter takes the best match. The arrow keys move through the list. Escape closes it. ＋ Create a new variable… opens the editor for that row. A new row joins the strategy only after you choose its source.

Built-in filters work offline and keep auto-run. A saved variable, measure or parameter changes the strategy to a variable strategy. The local service then calculates it, and auto-run pauses. Existing built-in filters move into the same list without change. A parameter becomes a one-term formula. A measure keeps its exact catalog revision. A variable row offers only the threshold units that fit its result. A built-in row keeps its own display unit. A new row starts with an empty value, and submission asks for each value. A changed source keeps the typed value. Edit formula opens the formula of that row. Use built-in strategy controls keeps built-in filters and removes variable filters. A message reports how many it removed.

Choose Create variable or Choose ranking variable beside the ranking controls. Give it a name. Build the formula in the editable equation. Select a parameter to replace it or change its settings. Use the operation buttons to add, subtract, multiply or divide the selected term. Division shows a stacked fraction. Select its bar to work with the whole group. Parentheses keep grouping explicit. Insert parameter opens the source picker for the selected position. Source insertion keeps the ranking or filter destination. A rejected Use shows an error and keeps the editor open. Undo and Redo restore equation edits. Only the selected term has form controls below the equation. Advanced JSON edits the same expression tree. Annual statistics require consecutive fiscal years. A month lookback reconstructs an earlier observation date. It does not create quarterly or TTM accounts.

The editor checks the formula after each pause in editing. The check uses the existing formula language, units and required inputs. A panel and the action bar show the state: checking, ready, formula incomplete or needs attention. An empty term shows formula incomplete and sends no request. A failure reports the expression path when a group, time rule or unit is invalid. Use and Save always check first. Input support does not guarantee availability for every company. Test on sample companies and Check data coverage are optional and start collapsed. Original sample preview evaluates only the 1–16 symbols and date that you request. Its explicit Original label is independent of the strategy execution choice. It shows available sample counts, original input dates, values and reasons. Preview makes no full-pool coverage claim and creates no backtest job.

The main button names its destination: Use for ranking, Add as filter or Update filter with the row number. Saving is optional. Save to My variables retains an immutable formula revision in the separate variable library. A loaded saved variable shows Save changes and Save as a new variable. A label states whether the variable is new, used by this strategy, saved, or saved with unsaved changes. Its tooltip keeps the exact identity. Favourite and Delete appear only for a saved variable. Names and favourites use an optimistic entry version. A concurrent change produces a conflict and keeps your local edit. The picker searches Favourites, My variables, parameters, measures and built-ins. Ranking, each condition and saved references share that picker. An exact old revision remains exact after a rename, edit or deletion. Saving a detached expression whose dependency is absent from the archive fails clearly; it does not silently import that dependency.

Use changes only the strategy draft. The selected source and highest or lowest direction stay visible. Filters keep their strict comparison, entered display threshold and canonical decimal threshold. Variable strategies require an explicit Screen latest or Run backtest. Variable strategies run with Original in all three scalar modes. A restored strategy that names the experimental engine shows the engine choice, so you can choose Original. The draft captures and restores that choice. Changing it does not relabel a displayed result or infer its producer. Every scalar result panel shows its recorded producer. Missing producer evidence stays explicitly unknown. Auto-run applies to the standalone built-in controls. Existing inclusive minimum-yield or maximum-multiple settings must be resolved explicitly before changing to scalar variables. The draft is kept when that transition cannot preserve meaning.

The draft captures complete program content, ordered roots and presentation before a manual or queue submission receives its retry identity. The editor and draft pack owner-produced editable definitions and names once per exact revision. Shared dependencies do not multiply the request size. Changed restored roots use the checked authoring projection. Unchanged captures retain their original complete content. An uncertain response retries the same payload. Later library changes cannot alter accepted work. A held queued edit protects its form until Save or Cancel ends that session. Ordinary result restoration uses that same protection.

Completed values, company explanations and downloads use the original immutable evidence. A selected-company trace follows its recorded scope, chunk, request and operation references. It shows captured arithmetic and financial input dates without calculating again. Complete original JSON is available under Advanced, and the complete evidence download keeps every original explanation. Reopening requires no current variable library or calculation.

variable_authoring.py owns financial-free authoring. The library owns exact raw snapshots and atomic saves. The definition owner converts checked detached programs into editable raw content with exact decimal compaction and revision checks. variable-workspace.js owns the shared editor and turns a list choice into an exact checked source. filter-picker.js owns searching and choosing in the filter list. range.js supplies the choices and owns the filter rows. StrategyDraft owns form sessions and submission capture. variable-evidence.js explains detached values; evidence-results.js presents bounded completed pages.

What does a submitted custom strategy retain?

Current source on main includes one variable workspace, complete strategy capture and Original scalar execution. Create and save variables, then choose exact revisions for ranking or filters. Run explicitly to calculate. Phase 6 is complete in source after independent audit and private verification. This source work does not change a running server. Original is the only engine the website runs. Native-cache coverage remains unknown.

Choose exact scalar sources→Capture program and labels→Normalize thresholds→Check complete request

Ranking and conditions can name an exact formula revision or a built-in scalar. Built-ins describe saved metric pairs or saved filter values. Yield and multiple remain independent saved values. No reciprocal is invented. Filters retain their original comparison scale. A custom condition also keeps its canonical decimal threshold and submitted display unit. For example, 8% is 0.08. A saved percent filter compares against 8 in its existing lane.

A custom ranking has an explicit highest or lowest direction. Inclusive ranks, selection order, pool and size or metadata bounds are captured. There is no hidden minimum-yield condition. Formula roots retain ranking-then-condition order, including repeated exact references. The complete variable program and presentation come from their existing capture owner.

backtest/application/strategy_requests.py owns the immutable strategy-capture/1 value. This namespaced format allocates no application result integer. require_strategy() checks restored content without a current library or display catalog. It preserves original labels after library edits or deletion. Current capability admission is separate. Unsupported experimental custom intent fails explicitly before financial work.

Submission equality includes the complete payload and presentation. Calculation equality excludes names, descriptive provenance, submitted threshold spelling and lowerable content bounds. Definition and display revisions, exact sources, direction and canonical thresholds still change calculation meaning. A retry must retain its original payload. It must not capture newer labels after an uncertain response.

A strategy capture allows at most 192 KiB of complete encoded content. A caller can lower this limit. The whole custom request allows at most 256 KiB, matching the existing queue ceiling. Names, display catalogs, presentation and escaped characters all count. The library's separate 3 MiB capture capability does not enlarge the application request. Excess content fails without truncation.

The captured-intent owner creates no worker or financial ownership. Original consumes it through the existing jobs, queue and result-access owners. The editor uses StrategyDraft for patches, held restoration and capture before submission identity. Existing records are not rewritten. Stored version-1/2/3 results retain their existing readers.

What reusable measures can a formula use?

Formulas can use 33 reusable measures. Each capture keeps exact definitions and its reachable dependencies. One program can contain at most 32 definitions. Positive division requires a positive denominator. Reported EBIT, free cash flow, debt and EPS retain their source fields. Report EBITDA uses accepted report history. Other legacy ratios retain the financial owners’ rules.

A latest root reads the stored latest owner lanes. Fixed and random roots, and preview roots on any historical session, January sessions included, use dated ownership, even on the same calendar date. A derived date uses dated ownership, even when its date equals the root date. A missing prepared company or lane does not fall back to a new calculation. Original is the only engine the website runs. The shared editor exposes expanded source choices through version-3 definitions. Original execution can use captured measures. Private synthetic checks do not establish installed-data coverage.

What annual growth can a formula calculate?

A formula can calculate growth or compound annual growth from 2 to 10 consecutive annual observations. The number of annual intervals is one less than the observation count. Each result is a scalar fraction: 0.1 means 10%. Every observation must be available. Growth requires a positive first value. Compound annual growth also requires a positive last value. An unavailable input or invalid endpoint produces an unavailable result.

Original execution supports these statistics in version 2 and 3 definitions. The shared editor exposes expanded source choices through version-3 definitions. Existing version 1 definitions and saved records keep their meaning.

How do custom variables run and retain their results?

Captured strategies use the local execution service in Latest, fixed dates and random dates. The shared editor supplies one captured strategy through the ordinary form. Built-in standalone screens keep their existing behavior. Original is the only engine the website runs. No running server or installed data changes from this source work.

Read complete prepared scope→Evaluate formula values→Rank once across the scope→Explain selected stocks→Close financial owners→Publish complete evidence

The SQLite observation view borrows Original's admitted connection. The column evaluator in backtest/variables/columns.py calculates formula values without step traces. It reads the typed facts in backtest/inputs/facts.py on the operation's research connection. Prepared latest owner lanes are the stored latest book rows. Latest roots use the typed latest admission. It loads the needed annual fields once for each company in the view. Income fiscal dates still define the annual spine. It uses one set of rules for anchors, annual members, dated lookups and owner measures, and binary64 arithmetic. After each scope, the view checks the research-file status and the admitted daily input identity. The evaluator owns reports and annual alignment. Dated scopes admit each book row with the view's admission rules: an eligible report, the legacy buffer, cached prices and an eligible valuation. Their enterprise value is the book's entry valuation. Latest and coverage scopes use the view’s root admission. Uncached companies keep their place in the original 250-candidate buffer. No formula expands the prepared universe. Scope receipts distinguish all source companies from prepared rows with usable return evidence. Their admission count applies only to those prepared rows.

With a built-in ranking and filter-first order, formulas run only for rows that are admitted, have a ranking value and pass every built-in condition and bound. No other row can be selected, so the holdings do not change. Other orders and formula rankings evaluate every row. The scalar policy allows at most 8,192 candidates in a scope. One global selection preserves directions, ties, selection order, original ranks and survivor weights. Missing ranking values exclude a company. Missing values affect only active conditions.

Built-in sources keep their actual saved values and comparison scale. Detached evidence records their declared canonical value too. In latest and fixed-date runs, the column evaluator also explains each selected stock. Its detail mode records the inputs, their fiscal, known and observation dates, reasons, source file digests and every operation, in the block shape that the evidence viewer reads. The same code computes the values that ranked the stock, so no second evaluator cross-checks them. A trace block larger than one evidence record is split in half. Older results keep their reference-evaluator explanations and open unchanged. Random-date runs keep each selected stock’s formula values and reasons without a step trace. Nothing invents a reciprocal yield. Generic holdings show ranking value, unit and direction. Actual prices, returns, exits and portfolio arithmetic stay with their existing owners.

Application artifact 4, scalar selected-book contract 2 and evidence codec 2 are separate allocations. They are not derived from a formula namespace. Old artifacts 1, 2 and 3 and codec 1 retain their meanings. The existing durable version-3 container stores either supported application/codec pair through explicit dispatch. Existing records are not migrated or rewritten.

Latest evidence is screen-only. It has zero trials and zero periods. It contains no future return or contribution. Latest cannot be saved as a historical backtest. Fixed and random dates reuse existing calendars, missing-book workers, parent-only writes, per-trial transactions and financial reduction. Original is the only engine the website runs. Unsupported experimental formula intent fails before readiness or financial work.

Complete evidence uses at most 256 MiB of encoded content. A record uses at most 8 MiB and a piece at most 1 MiB. A whole run has no task, inspected-row or scope ceiling. You can stop a run. Before a random-date or month-interval run starts, a size check estimates the stored result. It refuses a run whose estimate exceeds the writer’s byte bound. The writer’s bound still applies during the run. These are content limits, not measured process-memory claims. Exceeding a limit fails the request. No evidence is truncated and no partial completion is published.

Scalar failures retain a safe message, a code, an expression path and ordered validation issues. Ordinary submission errors and failed job or queue status use the same fields. Queue failure details survive restart. Legacy errors keep their original text and response shape.

Original sample preview checks an explicit request before financial ownership. Numerical sample preview fails before financial work. It observes only 1–16 named company/date roots. Its count describes those roots, not full-pool coverage. Preview creates no job and launches no backtest. A future nested date or invalid unit fails explicitly. Preview shows the requested sample count, captured values and units, unavailable reasons and original input dates. Recorded steps and complete JSON remain available. Editing, saving, favouriting, previewing and applying never launch a backtest.

Inspect recorded coverage is separate from sample preview. Choose a recorded latest date and pool from the admitted generation. The denominator is every snapshot row before formula availability, ranking, filters or rank ranges. Empty scopes have a zero denominator. Counts show valid and unavailable outputs. Provider admission failures and the first recorded formula failure reason are distinct. These reasons do not list every missing ingredient.

Inspection uses the same column evaluator. It creates no backtest, return book or saved result. A changed generation or absent scope fails the complete request. Results are never truncated. Recorded roots retain their stored owner lanes. Formula date shifts use dated policy, including equal dates. Inspection does not establish live-cache coverage or installed readiness.

Jobs automatically retain bounded evidence for a captured strategy. Queue receipts retain exact submitted programs, names and thresholds. Accepted retries keep the same payload. Later library edits and deletion cannot change it. A presentation-only waiting edit can retain its recorded random plan. A calculation change drops that plan. Replay compares calculation meaning without rewriting original plan bytes. An explicit Stop stays cancelled. Shutdown interruption returns work to waiting.

Completed views acquire the same immutable result owner as older results. Its limits remain 16 display readers and 32 active request pins. Bounded pages expose scopes, rows and explanations. Scope/chunk-qualified references remain unambiguous. Reopening uses no current library, catalog, preparation or calculation. Each request has an independent stream position.

The scalar CSV keeps original values, units, direction and explanation references. Download complete evidence to retain the full captured strategy, input identity and every explanation offline. That companion file contains the original checksummed framed bytes. Counted attachment lengths detect interrupted transfers. Financial views, connections and workers close before completion becomes visible.

Where do website and tool sources live?

website/browser/ holds plain scripts, styles and HTML fragments. website/rendering/ owns detached data, static markup, ordered assets, exports and build freshness. website/server/ owns HTTP adapters and server lifetime. The source-owning entries remain at their documented paths. Latest output stays self-contained.

tools/ops/ owns maintained operations. tools/experiments/ holds only the retained FMP API acquisition experiments: the probes, download_one and fetch_bulk. Thin documented commands call their real owners. The deployment entry can verify and start its implementation from the selected archive. This keeps an older controller able to install the new source layout. Historical evidence keeps its original paths and hashes.

The custom-variable program is complete and integrated into main. The source provides trusted prepared inputs and point-in-time formula evaluation. It provides immutable validation, typed-facts scalar evaluation and a separate durable variable library. It provides captured strategy intent, one shared workspace and ordinary Original execution with immutable evidence. It provides the separate complete semantic catalog and endpoint-aware annual and dated preparation, with all 52 direct inputs and the two adapters for formula evaluation. It provides reusable measures with bounded owner evidence, and shared authoring with recorded-scope coverage. Execution accepts the expanded captured vocabulary. The draft, editor, readable trace and bounded result presenter keep separate responsibilities. backtest/application/variable_coverage.py owns recorded-scope discovery and coverage reduction. backtest/application/scalar_execution.py owns the complete-scope read that inspection and selection share. backtest/variables/columns.py evaluates formula values for selection. Current built-in metric pairs keep their existing behavior. Read the current source map for the package owners.

What is the January record, and what checks the book code?

results/summary-exits.txt is the frozen record of the January study. It keeps a stock at its last price when trading stops. Nothing regenerates or changes it. results/baseline-history/, results/legacy/ and results/stops/ are frozen too. The legacy files use an older exit rule and are not the study result.

Preparation builds no January books and runs no second engine. The development check does that job on the real-data bench. python3 scripts/check.py runs one Original dated schedule: every 12 months from 1 January 1996 to 20 October 2026, legacy pool, EV/EBITDA ranks 1–50 and the default size floors. The end date is the frozen report's Through date. The check compares every book, holding, date, valuation, return and exit status with the independent reference engine at full precision. It also compares the annual rows with the frozen report at four decimals. It passes with zero differences in both comparisons.

Run the dated schedule→Run the reference engine→Compare at full precision→Zero differences

Every preparation is a full build. Research writes a temporary file and replaces the database in one step. A failure keeps the previous database.

How does the website adapt to a phone?

Desktop filters use four columns. Tablet filters use two columns. Phone filters use one column. Phone summary cards stack vertically. Buttons and form controls have a minimum height of 44 pixels.

Wide charts and tables scroll inside their panels. Scroll instructions remain visible. Stock symbols stay visible as stock tables scroll sideways. Tap a chart mark to read its detail below the chart. Mouse and keyboard interaction also work.

These layouts apply to latest picks, custom schedules and random trials. The built HTML includes the styles and interactions. Rebuild the website after a source change. A page already open in a browser needs a reload.

What do the charts and downloads show?

Browser downloads reflect the displayed result. Pending settings do not change a download. Historical views show period returns and the growth of an equal-weight portfolio.

A stock’s contribution is its holding return divided by the actual stock count. Gain and loss pies are scaled separately. Their slices are not shares of net return.

The return distribution chart shows trial counts for the current seed. CAGR and total return show strategy and paired SPY on the same bins and axes. You can also select the CAGR difference from SPY. Each series has its own mean marker. A dashed bell curve fits each series with nonzero standard deviation. This fit does not show that returns follow a normal distribution. Incomplete trials are excluded. Identical returns show one bar without a fitted curve.

The average random-trial CAGR is an average of trial results. It is not one portfolio return. Trial percentiles are not confidence intervals.

Which limits should I keep in mind?
  • The strategy uses equal starting weights and no commissions.
  • The saved-price group does not cover the full market.
  • Sector, exchange and listing status come from saved company metadata.
  • The 90-day report delay is an assumption. It is not a verified filing date.
  • Some supplier figures can include later revisions.
  • New early stops outside the original review can need further checks.

08 / Words used in this guide

The terms, without the code.

Cache
Saved data that the program can use again.
Book
The stock records for one buy date and one sell or mark date.
Pool / Stock group
The set of candidate stocks used for selection. It is separate from the final stock count.
Snapshot
A saved stock record for a particular date or holding period.
Filter
A condition that a stock must meet before ranking.
Rank
A stock’s position after filtering and sorting by the selected metric.
Rebalance
Select stocks again and give each selected stock the same starting weight.
Trial
One complete backtest with one set of sampled trade dates.
Seed / Date-set number
A number used to repeat random date choices with the same saved data and settings.
SQLite
A database engine that reads and writes local files. It does not need a separate database server.
Market cap
The estimated market value of the company’s equity.
EV / Enterprise value
In this model, estimated market cap plus report net debt.
EBITDA
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. The model derives it from saved annual metrics.
EBITDA/EV and EV/EBITDA
Reciprocal ratios. A higher positive EBITDA/EV means a lower positive EV/EBITDA.
P/B
Price divided by book value. This filter needs saved annual equity and a rebuild.
CAGR
The constant annual growth rate that would produce the same total growth over the test window.
SPY
The S&P 500 ETF used for comparison. Its saved return series includes dividends.
API / Local service
The browser’s way to ask Python for a dated calculation. These requests use saved data on your computer.
